A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. The main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reformatting and renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original MiniWoB++ and WorkArena experiments, including Llama and Qwen evaluations, compute-performance results and bootstrap analysis of 1,370 training configurations.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and additionally reports Qwen2.5 7B compute-performance curves in Figure 4.

M1.justification: Both versions specify the same SFT-to-on-policy pipeline, GRPO for Llama, RFT for Qwen, curriculum components and bootstrap Algorithm 1. The additional Qwen plot does not introduce a method component.

E1.justification: MiniWoB++, WorkArena, held-out goals and held-out tasks remain the evaluation coverage, with identical appendix task lists. Qwen was already evaluated in v2; its additional plot introduces no new dataset or task scenario.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains exactly the same proprietary baselines, teacher and student models, and pure RL, SFT and hybrid comparisons. Figure 4 introduces no new comparison method.

E3.justification: The stated splits, context limits, success-rate metric, checkpoint smoothing, model-selection procedures and FLOP accounting are unchanged. The Qwen curves extend reporting within the existing compute-allocation framework without specifying a different evaluation protocol.

E4.justification: New Figure 4 extends the analysis of compute allocation and SFT-to-on-policy branching to Qwen2.5 7B; v2 provided Qwen aggregate scores but only a Llama compute frontier. Existing hyperparameter, saturation, failure-case and entropy analyses remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Both retain 1,000 bootstrap resamples, 95% confidence intervals, Table 1 standard errors and the same run-selection and averaging descriptions. Figure 4 uses the existing two-seed averaging practice.

E6.justification: Figure 4 adds Qwen success-versus-compute trajectories for pure SFT and four on-policy starting points, showing compute advantages from warm-started training. All Table 1 values and pre-existing plotted results are unchanged; this is additional evidence, not a performance improvement between versions.

T1.justification: Equations 1–17 retain the same objectives, compute derivations and bootstrap maximum-statistic definitions and arguments. The bootstrap correctness discussion moves from Appendix J to K without substantive mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same central contributions: statistical diagnosis of 1,370 configurations, benefits of combining SFT with on-policy training, and matching peak SFT using 55% of its compute. The Qwen addition supports these retained claims.

C2.justification: Section 5 newly states that the compute-performance findings generalize to Qwen2.5 7B, referring to Figure 4. Existing explanations of saturation, environment shortcuts, hyperparameter effects and study limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The software stack, GPU allocations, preprocessing details, random-search ranges and selected hyperparameters are retained. No new code or data access instructions or substantive implementation details accompany the Qwen plot.

R1.justification: The same 30 referenced works and substantive related-work discussions are retained. Conversion to author–year citations and expanded author names changes presentation rather than research positioning.

P1.justification: v4 adds a Qwen appendix heading, cross-references and a short generalization statement, updates front matter and changes citation style. Most prose and the main section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v4 adopts a substantially different document-wide template, including a branded boxed first page, changed typography and spacing, and resized and repositioned displays. It adds Figure 4, separates the appendix heatmaps across pages, and moves the test-bootstrap figure to the final page.

improvement.justification: Figure 4 fills a limited evidence gap: v2 reported Qwen aggregate performance without showing its compute frontier. The added curves strengthen support for applying the compute-allocation advice beyond Llama. The core evidence remains intact, although moving the test-bootstrap figure far from its discussion slightly weakens navigation.
